findings.issue: _pool module-level singleton leak: after live-DB tests set _pool, the 'Route registration (no-DB)' test deletes DATABASE_URL and creates a new server, but getPool() returns the already-set _pool instead of throwing HttpError(503). Result: test gets 404 (static handler PUT-reject) instead of 503. Fails only in full suite run, passes in isolation.
findings.suggestion: Move 'Route registration (no-DB)' test to the TOP of the file (before any live-DB tests that trigger getPool()), or export resetPoolForTesting() from registry-defs.ts and call it in the test's setup.

findings.issue: kind:'noop' is defined in UpdateSchemaResult union and handled in response logic (lines 399-404) but updateSchemaInTx never returns it. The 'unchanged schema' path documented in the comment ('If record_schema is absent or unchanged → 200 { updated: false }') is not implemented — an identical schema still triggers a DB UPDATE and returns {updated:true}.
findings.suggestion: Either remove 'noop' from the union and delete the dead branch, or add JSON.stringify equality check before applying UPDATE.

findings.issue: AC-13 (partial failure → ROLLBACK) is listed in the file header as covered but no live test exists. Rollback correctness of the force path on appendAuditEvent failure is not verified by a live-DB probe.
findings.suggestion: Add a live-DB test that simulates appendAuditEvent throwing; verify record_schema, stale, and tier remain unchanged.

findings.issue: SET LOCAL choros.promoting='1' is issued before the soft-path early return (if destructiveDeps.length === 0). The GUC is harmless but unnecessary in the soft path — misleads readers about why it is set.
findings.suggestion: Move the SET LOCAL choros.promoting='1' into the force path block (7b), after the soft-path early return.

findings.issue: Per-dep and per-page UPDATE loops issue one SQL statement per affected dep/page (N+1 roundtrips). Not harmful at MVP scale but inefficient at large dep counts.
findings.suggestion: Replace loops with unnest-based batch UPDATEs for production readiness.
